description: For a repository that pins a container image the org's image pipeline released: any tfvars line of the form <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/<repository>:run-<run id>@sha256:<digest> is a dependency whose versions are the release repository's run-<id> tags, ordered by run id, since run ids only increase and commit hashes do not sort. The digest is what runs; the run tag is there to order by. A consumer's pins move together in one pull request on a stable branch, outside the non-major batch, with no release age and no dashboard approval, since the images are the consumer's own and their tests already ran. A new run id reads as a major to the regex versioning, which is why the dashboard rule is overridden here, and run ids are hundreds of millions apart, which is why the limit on how far a major may jump is lifted for them. The workflow that runs this needs the release-read role (renovate.yml's aws_role_arn).

customManagers.description: The pin, wherever a tfvars file writes it. depName is the repository URL, currentValue the run tag and currentDigest the digest, so an update moves both.

packageRules.description: One pull request per consumer for its image pins, on renovate/major-image-pins since every new run id is a major, at once and without the dashboard. Only the pins: an ECR image another manager finds keeps the shared rules.
